newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse turnover higher on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse turnover higher on foreign buying.

text.p: Activity at the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) improved on Wednesday, boosted by foreign investor buying, brokers and bourse officials said.

Turnover was 13.362 million shillings on 363,382 shares from 11.685 million shillings on 326,448 shares on Tuesday. The overall market was still down, with the 20-share index sliding 10.23 points to stand at 2997.44.

Foreign investors bought 70,400 shares of Uchumi Supermarket at 45 from 45.50, some 31,000 shares of Kenya Commercial Bank at between 56 and 57.50 from 57, 10,600 shares of Kenya Breweries at between 47.75 and 48.50 from 48.25 and 4,500 shares of Firestone East Africa at between 25-26.50 from 24.75.
One broker said the strong foreign interest in Uchumi Supermarket and Kenya Commercial Bank was from a large buying order that was maintaining the price at current levels.
But another broker differed, saying the strong buying order from foreigners in what were perceived to be government firms was a unique feature demonstrating confidence in the market.
Kenya Airways share touched 8.95, the lowest since they first traded on the market on June 3. The airline announced an interim dividend of 25 cents on November 19.
"Most shareholders were disappointed because they expected at least a minimum dividend of 1.0," a senior broker said.
"I think most speculators will opt to get out of the share, but the share still remains good for long term investors."

On average prices of key shares reflected the bearish mood of the market. Kenya National Mills eased to 45.25 from 45.50 while British American Tobacco Kenya closed at 62.50 from 63. Total Kenya traded unchanged at 62.

"Two weeks ago, all share prices were going down consistently, now at least some are picking," one broker said. "We hope to see some change in market sentiment especially with corporate bonds scheduled for trading early next month."
Corporate bonds will begin trading at the secondary market on December 2, 1996.
